- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, it often overcorrects; cap forecast peak at 1–2% above recent high.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed; apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum, not just price history.
- When sentiment is high and price is near recent high, model often overreaches; apply mean reversion bias: cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 5-day high.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and price is rising, model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–4% in final 5–7 days.
